question: Do wrist-worn accelerometer measures of physical activity and sleep predict later disease and death? Need thousands of adults, wrist placement, linked hospital/diagnosis/death outcomes; US university.

requirements.text: Wrist-worn device, several days to a week or more
At least a few thousand adults
Linked follow-up: hospital records, diagnoses or death registration
Wrist placement (comparable with other wrist studies)

access.evidence: NHANES public-use files; linked mortality public-use files are downloaded from CDC FTP (page: no registration mentioned)

problems: the page is titled "PAXHD_G", which does not name "NHANES 2011-2014 wrist accelerometer (PAXMIN/PAXDAY)"; only words in its text or address match, so check that this page is the dataset you meant
notes: access tier unknown: no registry metadata states it; read the landing page before calling the data open

sentences: This file contains one record for each eligible participant.
Not every eligible NHANES participant has a data file.
These variables in the hour summary file (PAXHR_G) indicate the number of valid minutes in the hour by algorithm assigned PAM wearing status.
These variables in the day summary file (PAXDAY_G) indicate the number of valid minutes in the day by algorithm assigned PAM wearing status.

datasets.why: Open now: ActiGraph GT3X+ on the non-dominant wrist for 7 days (2011-2014, US national sample), linkable to NDI mortality.

R1.evidence: Search result summarising CDC documentation: ActiGraph GT3X+, non-dominant wrist, 7 days

R2.evidence: One published analysis used 3,032 adults aged 50+; total adult N not confirmed by me

R3.evidence: Death only (NDI). No hospital or diagnosis outcomes in public-use files; restricted RDC files exist

access_steps: Download PAX files (2011-12 "G", 2013-14 "H") from CDC NHANES pages
Download public-use linked mortality files from CDC FTP (ftp.cdc.gov, datalinkage/linked_mortality)
Merge on SEQN; apply survey weights
caveats: Mortality only; the page says LMFs were updated through 31 Dec 2022 but the public-use end date is not stated there (a paper cites follow-up through 2019)
Restricted-use linked files need an NCHS RDC application

datasets.why: Largest US source with linked EHR outcomes: Fitbit (wrist) activity and sleep for ~59,000 participants, ~22,000 with EHR and 6+ months of data in one study.

R1.evidence: Consumer Fitbit, participant-supplied, months to years of data; not a research-grade accelerometer

R2.evidence: 59,000 with Fitbit data; 22,019 with EHR and >=6 months (Hou et al.)

R3.evidence: EHR diagnoses (incident disease studies published); death data less certain, unconfirmed

access_steps: Check your institution has a DURA (Register page, researchallofus.org)
If not, ask your institutional signing official to sign one
Create account, verify identity (Login.gov/ID.me), complete Responsible Conduct of Research training, sign Data User Code of Conduct
Analyse inside the cloud Researcher Workbench
caveats: Metrics from consumer trackers are not directly comparable with ACC research-grade (GGIR) outputs
Fitbit users are a self-selected subset

datasets.why: Gold standard for this question: Axivity AX3 wrist, 7 days, ~100,000 people, linked hospital records, cancer and death registers. But new applications are reported paused.

R1.evidence: UKB documentation: Axivity AX3 wrist-worn, 7 days

R3.evidence: Incident disease and mortality used in the cited papers

access_steps: Register your institution/researcher account on the UK Biobank AMS
Submit an application with research proposal
If approved, pay fee and sign the MTA within 90 days; analyse in the Research Analysis Platform (DNAnexus)
caveats: Per search results (not confirmed on UKB pages, which blocked my tools): applications paused since April 2026, aim to reopen late 2026; RAP closed for some time
Fee per search of fees page: Tier 1 £3,000 for 3 years (+VAT); RAP compute extra

datasets.why: 7-day wrist Actiwatch Spectrum in 2,156 multi-ethnic US adults (2010-2013), followed for CVD events and death.

not_recommended.name: Hip-worn cohorts (e.g. NHANES 2003-06, WHI OPACH, Women's Health Study)
not_recommended.reason: From memory: hip-worn, fail the wrist requirement.

gaps: Whitehall II (GENEActiv wrist, 2012/13) and Rotterdam Study (GENEActiv wrist) exist but I did not confirm sample sizes, outcome linkage or access terms beyond contact routes.

notes: Registries searched were general-purpose; the main cohorts were found by web search and literature. UK Biobank pause is reported by search results, unconfirmed on its own site.
